The v items are the IPIP-VIA adaptations, hosted on ipip.ori.org as IPIP scales under that statement; the s items are IPIP-format rewordings of Torrubia et al.'s SPSRQ administered in the OPAS mailing; n = BRI revision of the CES-D; b = Goldberg's Curious Experiences Survey (DES-derived). public_note: This table pools three response formats under resp 1-5: most items use the IPIP accuracy scale, but n1-n24 are the Behavioral Report Inventory's past-week frequency items (the same responses as goldberg_2018_bri_feel) and b1-b31 are the Curious Experiences Survey frequency items (the same responses as BRI curio1-curio31), and item v30 was administered as 'Have created something of beauty in the last year', the reverse of the wording on the IPIP website.

note: Item codes r_ods001..r_ods144 are the S1 Appendix .xls column names, melted unchanged by data/hermans_2015_dm1_rods.py; the paper's S1 Appendix legend labels all 105 codes by name ('r_ods001 = bend and pickup' ... 'r_ods144 = make a telephone call'), 105/105 matching the live item set, and item_text is that legend verbatim (HTML entities </> decoded to </>). Legend labels are terse descriptions, not the administered question wording; the stem 'Are you able to...' in instructions is taken from S1 Fig / Table 2 (the final 25-item DM1-Activ C form), which Methods says were the instructions given for this administration ('see S1 Fig for an overview of the guidelines/instructions'). Anchors are S1 Fig's column headers verbatim (Impossible to perform (0) / Able to perform, but with difficulty (1) / Able to perform, without difficulty (2)); Methods words them 'unable to perform (0) ... without any difficulty (2)'. Source defect overridden: the S1 Appendix legend says '3 = able to perform, without difficulty', but the raw .xls holds only 0/1/2 (5379/7880/18716 cells) and both Methods and S1 Fig code that anchor as 2, so it ships at resp=2. Methods also says 'not applicable' was scored 3; no 3 occurs in the raw file. Language: participants were Dutch DM1 patients recruited via the Dutch neuromuscular patients' association (Maastricht); the paper never names the administration language, so language=Dutch is an inference. No Dutch text in the paper, S1 Fig or S1 Appendix (the only supplements), so the English base fields are the fallback, translation_source=study_supplied. Rights: S1 Fig marks the form 'DM1-ACTIVC(c)' - a bare copyright notice, no fee/NC/ND/redistribution clause found in the paper or S1 Fig. The S1 Fig caption 'For further instructions to translate the obtained ordinal scores to an interval (Logits) scores, please contact the authors' concerns obtaining a scoring conversion, not use or redistribution of the wording, so it reserves no right over the text; not in instrument_rights_register.csv; no register row written.
